brief: Tonight is Push B, and it is the first one since 2 September — your only Push B at the new gym, and the night you had to improvise half of it. Two lifts go up, three get their rep target lowered to something you have actually hit, and one comes down a long way on purpose. The overhead press: there is no smith machine here, so this is the dumbbells, and 45 is finished — you pressed it for eight three times on 2 September and for nine three times on 8 September. Tonight opens at 45 for eight, then three sets of the 50s for six. You have touched the 50s once, for five reps, as a tired fourth set — so six is one more than you have ever done, three times over. That is the hardest ask on the card and it is deliberate: this is the last hard week before the deload on 21 September, and the rack has nothing between 45 and 50. The chest press goes to 165 on the two work sets, opening at 157.5. On 8 September you pressed 157.5 for eleven and then for ten, both at or past the top of this slot's range, and 165 is the smallest step that stack makes. Note the opener is heavier than last time's opener — if it does not move, log what you did. The cable crossover reads 15, not 25. Your own note from 2 September says that 25 was dumbbell flyes, so repeating it would put a dumbbell number on a cable stack. The one real reading of this gym's crossover is 8 September, where you did 15 for thirteen twice. If the crossover is occupied and you do dumbbell flyes again instead, take the 20s — the 25s put you under the rep floor last time. Three lifts keep their weight and get an honest rep number instead of one you keep missing: lateral raises at 15 for fourteen, rear-delt flies at 100 for thirteen then twelve, and the overhead triceps at 55, 55, then 52.5 on the last set so all three land in range instead of collapsing on the third. The reverse-grip pushdown takes the smallest step the cable can make, 28.75. Dips are a blank: you have not done them since 23 August at the old gym and they were skipped entirely on 2 September, so nobody knows whether this building has an assist machine. Tonight is the reading — three sets of twelve at bodyweight, and if the machine is not there, log what you did instead. Two things from last night that are still open. Your leg extension reading worked exactly as intended — you logged 125 and 140 where the card suggested 105 and 135, so that machine now has a real number. But the hip abductor came in at 110 when the card asked 142.5, and you closed 135 on 5 September on Legs B. That is a big gap and nobody here can explain it — if the Legs A abductor is a different machine from the Legs B one, say so in a note and both days stop guessing. Last, the clock. Push B as written is 24 sets and you have been finishing 17 to 21, with the lift at the end of the card always the one that gets dropped. Nothing tonight adds a set. If the clock beats you, protect the overhead press and the chest press — those two are the only things being tested.

flags.note: No review ran yesterday, 13 September — the automatic job did not commit. You trained Legs A on the packet written on the 12th, which was the right session, so nothing was wrong; but the app showed you a two-day-old review date and that is why.

Five Yes/No cards are waiting. Three have been unanswered since 11 September: drop the hanging leg raise from Legs A, rename the Push B opener to the dumbbell press you actually do, and drop the cable lateral raise from Push A. Two are new tonight.

Answer the shoulder-press card AFTER tonight, not during. Accepting it renames tonight's opener slot, and the moment it does, tonight's 45-and-50s numbers stop applying and you drop back to the app's own.

Tonight's rear-delt fly card asks three sets and one of the new Yes/No cards asks to make it two from now on. That is not a contradiction: tonight follows the program as it stands, and the card decides what happens after.
Your recovery trainer vetoed any weight increase on the overhead triceps and I upheld it. The third set has failed at 55 twice running, so tonight that set drops to 52.5 instead.
Push B as written is 24 sets. You have been finishing 17 to 21, and the lift last on the card is always the one that goes. Nothing tonight adds a set.

Two asks tonight sit above anything you have done at this gym: three sets of the 50-lb dumbbells for six on the overhead press, and 165 on the chest press. Both were argued against by your recovery trainer and both stand. Coming up short is information, not failure.
Nobody knows whether this gym has an assisted dip machine. It was skipped on 2 September with no note and has not been done since 23 August. Log whatever you find, including nothing.

Last night's hip abductor went in at 110 where the card asked 142.5 and where you closed 135 on 5 September. If Legs A and Legs B use different abductor machines, one note from you fixes both days permanently.

Bodyweight was last logged 23 August at 207, twenty-two days ago and flat before that. The show is 1 March. Your recovery trainer judged it does not change tonight's numbers, but says nobody can tell whether the gym change came with under-eating until you weigh in.
Meso 2, week 4 of 4 — the last hard week. The deload starts 21 September. Three trainers reported, six disagreements settled, one fatigue veto upheld, no pain or injury objection.

proposals.why: Your two leg days run the same lifts from the fourth one on, so Legs A gives up the hanging leg raise and keeps the cable crunch while Legs B keeps both, which finally makes the two days different.

On 2 September you pressed dumbbells in this slot and wrote "New gym. No smith machine. Dumbbell press", so the Push B opener takes the name of the lift you are actually doing and asks for 4 sets of 8 to 10 instead of the smith bar's 6 to 8 — the name and the rep ask change, nothing else.

This has sat at the same 10 pounds since the middle of August without the reps ever climbing, and Push B already gives you three sets of dumbbell lateral raises, which is the lift you told us on 23 August you thought was getting too many sets for such a small muscle.

You finished 12 reps — the top of this slot's range — on every set the last two times you did dips, and because the slot carries no weight there is nothing else that can go up, so this raises the range to 12 to 20 reps and makes reps the thing that climbs.

Push B asks for 24 sets a night and the one you keep leaving behind is the third set of reverse pec deck — two sets on 23 August, two again on 2 September, and the last time you did three was 3 August — so this makes the written ask two sets instead of three.

overrides.reason: No smith machine here, so this is the dumbbells. 45 is finished — eight reps three times on 2 September, nine reps three times on the 8th. The 50s have been tried once, for five, as a tired fourth set; six reps is one more than you have ever done there. Last hard week before the deload, and the rack has nothing between 45 and 50.

On 8 September you pressed 157.5 for eleven and then for ten, both at or past the top of this range, so 165 is earned and it is the smallest step this stack makes. The opener is heavier than last time's opener — if it does not move, log what you actually did.

Not done since 23 August, and skipped entirely on your one Push B here, so nobody knows if this gym has the machine. Tonight is the reading: three sets of twelve at bodyweight. If the machine is not here, log what you did instead and say so.

Dumbbells weigh the same at both gyms, so 15 stays. The app would ask fifteen reps on the top sets and you got twelve and thirteen on 2 September — fourteen beats that honestly, and holding fifteen there is what earns the 17.5s.

Your note says the 25 on 2 September was dumbbell flyes, not this machine, so repeating it would put a dumbbell number on a cable stack. The only real reading here is 8 September: 15 for thirteen, twice. If the crossover is taken and you do dumbbell flyes instead, use the 20s — the 25s put you under the rep floor.

The app would print fifteen reps at 100; you got thirteen on 2 September and twelve and twelve on the 8th, so the weight stays and the rep number says what is actually being asked. The third set is written because the program still calls for three — one of tonight's Yes/No cards asks whether to make it two from now on.

This is the lift that falls over at the end of the night: 55 went eleven, ten, nine on 8 September, and on the 2nd you dropped the last set to 50 yourself. No weight increase — your recovery trainer vetoed that and I upheld it. First two sets hold at 55, the third drops one notch to 52.5 so all three land in range.

This has climbed cleanly and carried across the move: 23.75, then 25, then 27.5 for fifteen and fourteen on 2 September — the top of the range on the first set. 28.75 is the smallest real step this cable makes. It also sits last on the card, which is where you run out of time, so if you only get one set, make it count.

dissent.progression: 45 is finished — open there for eight, then three sets of the 50s for six.
dissent.recovery: Hold all four sets at 45; the one attempt at 50 gave five reps, under the six-rep floor.
dissent.why: Recovery is right that 50 has never been completed in range, but that single attempt was a fourth set after three sets of 45, and on 8 September he pressed 45 for nine three times on the other push day. The rack has no weight between 45 and 50, so holding means standing still on a lift that is demonstrably done with 45. This is the last hard week before the 21 September deload, which is exactly when to spend the attempt rather than bank it.

dissent.progression: Open 157.5 for ten, then two sets at 165 — he beat the rep ceiling at 157.5 on 8 September.
dissent.recovery: Cap at 157.5 and add nothing; the light openers on 2 September were him finding the scale, not real work.
dissent.why: Recovery's reading of the 2 September openers is correct and I used it — that is why the ramp is gone. But it then caps at a weight he pressed for eleven reps on 8 September, one past the top of this slot's range. Beating the ceiling is the whole trigger for adding load, and 165 is the smallest step the stack makes, so refusing it would be a hold with no reason behind it.

dissent.progression: Prescribe the cable at 15 — the 8 September reading is the only genuine one from this gym's crossover.
dissent.recovery: Prescribe 20-lb dumbbells, because he substituted dumbbell flyes here on 2 September and went under the rep floor with the 25s.
dissent.why: Both seats agree the 25 was a dumbbell number and must not be repeated. They split on which hardware tonight is. On 8 September he used this gym's crossover cable for the low-to-high version, which proves the machine exists and he can get on it — the 2 September substitution was his first night in the building. The card names a cable crossover, so it gets a cable number, and I put recovery's 20-lb dumbbell answer in the card's own text as the fallback if the machine is occupied.

dissent.progression: Three sets at 100, reps written as thirteen, twelve, twelve instead of the app's fifteen.
dissent.recovery: Same weight, but only two sets — he has taken two on each of the last two push days and asking for a third is asking for a set he will not do.
dissent.why: Both agree on 100 and both agree fifteen reps is not real. On the third set I ruled for progression because the program as it stands says three, and quietly printing two would change his program by attrition rather than by decision. The program trainer raised exactly this tonight as a Yes/No card asking to make it two from now on — so the third set stays written tonight and he gets to actually decide it, instead of it being decided for him.

dissent.progression: Hold 55 on the first two sets and drop the third to 52.5 so all three land inside the rep range.
dissent.recovery: Hold 55 on all three sets and add nothing until all three come back in range; vetoed any increase on fatigue grounds.
dissent.why: The veto was against adding load, and nothing here adds load — progression's call goes down, not up. Recovery's own evidence is that the third set fails at 55: he dropped it to 50 himself on 2 September and got nine reps on the 8th. Repeating 55 a third time would prescribe the failure again on purpose, so the third set comes down one notch. The veto is upheld, not overridden.

dissent.progression: Take the 1.25-lb micro to 28.75 — 27.5 gave fifteen reps, the top of the range.
dissent.recovery: Hold 27.5, because this sits last on the card and the last lift is where he runs out of time.
dissent.why: Recovery's point is real but it is about the clock, not the load, and the answer to running out of time is not to freeze the weight forever. He earned the step by hitting the top of the range, and 28.75 is the smallest increase this cable can physically make. I carried the timing concern into the card's own text instead.
